stem: A technician uses the same scissors on plants in several rooms without following a sanitation procedure. What is the main concern?
choices: Repeated cutting can leave sap on the blades, making later cuts less precise even when the tool remains within one crop area
The scissors can act as a pathway for moving pests or pathogens between plants and rooms
Repeated use can change wound size between plants, which may alter how quickly cut surfaces dry after the work is completed
Moving tools between rooms can mix plant residues on shared work surfaces, creating a documentation concern even when no biological transfer occurs
rationale: Shared tools can act as fomites and transfer biological material between plants or rooms when sanitation procedures are not followed, making tool hygiene part of the facility's biosecurity system.
